I have answered questions from global audiences for fifteen years, and my first rule is simple. Before you answer, say the question back in your own words. So what you are asking is whether the cost goes up next year. It takes three seconds, and it does three things. It shows respect. It checks that you understood, which matters a lot when people have different accents. And it gives your brain a moment to find the answer. Half the bad answers I have heard in my career were good answers to a question nobody asked.

I work in Munich, and I will be honest. When I ask a question and the person repeats it back to me, I feel that we are losing time. I know what I asked. I want the answer. If you are not sure you understood, ask me one short thing: do you mean this year or next year? That is fine. But do not repeat my whole question to me like a report. Answer first, then explain. In a meeting with ten people, every repeated question costs a minute, and the minutes add up.
